english: A box that will auto-sort items placed inside of it into nearby matching containers.

A Round World is a light-touch quality of life pack. It adds no new mechanics of its own - nearly everything here is an existing SCore feature switched on, plus one new craftable container.

Nothing alters the game's rules or progression. Recipes, perks, loot, gamestage and difficulty are all left alone, so it can be dropped onto an otherwise vanilla game without changing how that game plays.

SCore must be installed. Every feature described on these pages is implemented there; this modlet only turns them on.

Crafting reads from nearby containers. Ingredients sitting in storage near you count toward a recipe, so materials no longer have to be hauled into your own inventory first.

Block upgrades and repairs read from containers too, so the same convenience applies while you are patching a wall or upgrading a frame.

With one deliberate exception: upgrading and repairing are blocked while enemies are near. Shoring up a base is something you do between fights rather than during one.

The Drop Box is a new container that sorts for you. Anything placed inside is moved out into nearby containers that already hold that item, so unloading after a run is one drop rather than a sorting session.

It comes in three tiers. The wood box costs 10 wood, 5 nails, 10 mechanical parts and 10 electrical parts. Upgrade it with 10 forged iron and then 10 forged steel, or craft any tier outright by swapping the wood for that metal.

Reading is shared across your party. When one member reads a book, everyone in the party receives the benefit, so a group no longer needs to find and hoard duplicate copies of the same volume.\n\nChallenges redeem themselves. Completed challenges pay out as you finish them, with no trip back to the challenge window to claim each one.

Zombies vary their walk. Instead of everything sharing one animation, zombies draw from the available walk types, so a crowd reads as individuals rather than a formation.

Whatever you are aiming at shows a health bar, so you can see how much fight is left in a target instead of guessing.

Flickering prefab lights are switched off. The strobing lights found in some points of interest hold steady instead.
